name: Eastern Dandenong Ranges Trail
reason: Wikivoyage lists a 17 km trail that simply follows the Puffing Billy line: part of a larger spot already kept, a linear route.

name: Ferntree Gully National Park
reason: Wikivoyage treats it as part of Dandenong Ranges National Park; the walks (Kokoda Track) are separate spots. Park inside park.

name: Sherbrooke Forest
reason: Wikivoyage names Sherbrooke Forest as the forest behind Belgrave; well-known lyrebird walks, a second-tier nature stop. Parks Victoria page unreachable (not evidence against).

name: Kallista
reason: Wikivoyage line only describes houses and gardens; a village with no named sight.

name: Gembrook
reason: Town at the Puffing Billy terminus; the railway is the draw and is its own spot; no distinct sight.

name: Lysterfield Lake Park
reason: Wikivoyage lists Lysterfield Lake; regional park with lake, walking and cycling trails, over half an hour. Kept as the single Lysterfield spot.

name: Yarra Ranges Regional Museum
reason: For: open museum in a purpose-built Lilydale building, tourism-board listed. Against: one source, a regional museum, short visit.

name: Ada Tree
reason: Giant mountain ash after a short walk in Yarra Ranges forest, named by Visit Yarra Valley; a distinct natural landmark guides single out. Visit Yarra Valley page not re-opened; earlier counted source accepted.

name: Mont De Lancey Historic Homestead
reason: For: historic homestead open to public with cafe, tourism-board listed. Against: one source, small local heritage site.

name: Ngurrak Barring Art Trail
reason: Dispersed public-art trail linking villages, not one place to spend half an hour; no single stop.

name: Yarra Valley Railway
reason: Wikivoyage names the heritage railway at Healesville; the ride is the attraction, a permanent venue (runs weekends and holidays).

name: Four Pillars Gin Distillery
reason: Two Wikivoyage mentions; distillery tastings and tours are a recognised attraction like a brewery tour.

name: Maroondah Reservoir Park
reason: Wikivoyage names it, 5 km east of Healesville; reservoir park with picnic area, walks and lookout.

name: Domaine Chandon
reason: Well-known sparkling winery with tastings, named by Wikivoyage; winery is a recognised visitor draw.

name: Yering Station
reason: Victoria's oldest vineyard with historic buildings, cellar door and restaurant, a headline Yarra Valley winery in every guide. Wikivoyage page did not list it; guidebook-level knowledge, source not opened.

name: Coombe Yarra Valley Melba's Garden Walk
reason: Century-old Melba estate gardens open to visitors, tourism-board listed; a garden walk is a half-hour-plus visit.

name: CherryHill Orchards
reason: Seasonal pick-your-own and farm shop; a shop/farm gate rather than a distinct permanent sight.

name: Trees Adventure Glen Harrow Park
reason: Wikivoyage Dandenong Ranges lists the ropes and zipline park; a permanent paid activity venue of hours.

name: Beeches Rainforest Walk
reason: Wikivoyage lists a short rainforest walk off Lady Talbot Drive; a named walk worth 30+ min.

name: Masons Falls
reason: Wikivoyage Kinglake names the falls and 700 m walk in Kinglake National Park; a classic short waterfall walk.

name: Wombelano Falls
reason: Wikivoyage Kinglake calls it a stunning hidden gem with an easy walk; second-tier waterfall stop.

name: South Jawbone Peak
reason: Visit Yarra Valley names the 3.5 km summit hike; a named peak walk.

name: Lake Eildon National Park
reason: National park with Lake Eildon boating, camping and walking; Parks Victoria page unreachable but a national park is a second-tier stop and park rule makes it its own spot.

name: Peninsula Tunnels
reason: For: gold-era river diversion tunnels, walkable heritage site near Warburton. Against: one source, niche, short visit.

name: Wirrawilla Rainforest Walk
reason: Visit Yarra Valley calls it an easy short rainforest circuit in Toolangi State Forest; a named walk.

name: Toolangi State Park
reason: Wrapper for the forest whose walk (Wirrawilla) is kept; Discovery Centre alone is minor.

name: O'Shannassy Aqueduct Trail
reason: Visit Yarra Valley describes a 30 km walking and cycling trail along a historic aqueduct; a promoted trail.

name: Lysterfield Lake
reason: Duplicate of Lysterfield Lake Park (same place).
